source_refs.note: Wall of the Heart: a main subheading of 11.1 Structure and functioning of the heart, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 235-236.

blocks.text: The wall of heart is composed of three layers. The inner layer of pericardium i.e., epicardium makes the outer lining of heart wall. Beneath epicardium, there is the thickest layer of heart wall i.e., myocardium. Myocardium is made of cardiac muscles. Endocardium is present beneath myocardium. It is a single layer of epithelial cells and make the inner linings of heart chambers (Figure 11.1).

blocks.alt: Left: the heart inside its pericardial sac, with a small box marked on its wall. Centre: the box enlarged as layers: the fibrous pericardium, then the serous pericardium, made of the parietal pericardium and the visceral pericardium with pericardial fluid between them. Right: a block of the heart wall with the visceral pericardium outside, the thick myocardium of muscle fibres and the endocardium inside, and the pericardial fluid and parietal pericardium beyond.
blocks.caption: Figure 11.1: Pericardium and heart wall (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 11.1).
